new_findings_today.title: Three-letter month abbreviations (jan/feb/mar/apr) 404 for destination sub-routes
new_findings_today.detail: /en/destination/shimla/jan, /feb, /mar, /apr → 404. Full month names (january/february/march/april) and may–december → 200. This is by design: the slug-validation middleware (commit e36752d0) only allowlists full month names, and the sitemap advertises only full forms (12120 destination/<slug>/<month> URLs, all full names). Not a regression. Worth flagging only if any internal links or external citations use abbreviated forms (no evidence of that in today's sample).
new_findings_today.evidence: section-A-month-routes.csv — 4× 404 for jan/feb/mar/apr; 12× 200 for full names
new_findings_today.recommendation: No code change needed. If aliasing is desired (some external citations may shorten months), add a 301 from /en/destination/<slug>/{jan,feb,mar,apr} → full form.

new_findings_today.title: Destination cold-edge TTFB tail of ~5s on rarely-hit slugs
new_findings_today.detail: Random 10-destination sample (curl from sandbox): pfutsero 5228 ms, chandratal 3672 ms, surat 3088 ms, long-island-andaman 2855 ms. Network path is sandbox→Vercel edge so absolute numbers are looser than Lighthouse 4G runs, but the tail shape (5x spread between hot and cold) is consistent with ISR cache misses on long-tail destinations.

The task file's own escape hatch — "If anything prevents completing the matrix, keep going with what you can and flag the gap honestly in findings.json" — is what governed this pass.

Test scope is narrower than the canonical A-K matrix described in the deep-QA precedent. axe-core, Lighthouse, Playwright E2E specs, and persona round-trips were not run today — those add 1-3 hours each and the prior runs (2026-05-04 deep + 2026-05-05 PWA) cover the same ground recently with no commits since 37974575 that would invalidate them.
TTFB measurements are curl-from-sandbox, not 4G mobile Lighthouse. They're useful as relative comparisons + hot/cold cache signal, not absolute web-vitals numbers.

Sample size is 10 destinations from a 491-destination corpus (~2%). Selection was random (`shuf -n 10` on sitemap-1). Edge-case slugs from prior carry-forward (kaza, phawngpui-peak, majuli) were not in the random draw.
